\[
R'_c = R_c \left[\log\left(\alpha\, (I_c + 1)\right) - \log \sum_{j} (I_j + 1)\right],
\qquad \alpha = 125
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(R_c\): The multi-scale Retinex of channel c
- \(\alpha\): The constant of the color restoration
- \(I_j\): The red, green and blue values of the pixel, 0 to 255

R_c is the multi-scale Retinex of channel c with the scales sigma_1, sigma_2 and sigma_3 and equal weights. Jobson, Rahman and Woodell multiply it by the color restoration function beta log(alpha I'_c). Here I'_c = I_c / sum_j I_j is the channel's share of the pixel. They use alpha = 125, beta = 46 and the scales 15, 80 and 250, then a gain G = 192 and an offset b = -30. Petro, Sbert and Morel found that no fixed gain and offset suits all images, and stretch each channel with Simplest Color Balance instead. That stretch removes any common factor, so beta, G and b have no effect here. They also warn that the restoration can invert colors where a channel is near 0, because both factors are then negative. PixelNexus takes the log of I + 1 so that black pixels have a finite log, and a result with no spread turns mid gray.
